Compare incidence or mortality rates

Source: R/compare_rate.R
compare_rate.Rd

Compare a registry rate with an external CI5-style reference rate using the standard errors of the two rates. The test is performed on the logarithm of the rate ratio, so the null hypothesis is that the rate ratio equals one.

Usage

compare_rate(
  x,
  event = c("inci", "mort"),
  standard = "wld85",
  reference = NULL,
  rate_col = NULL,
  se_col = NULL,
  variance_col = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  multiplier = 1e+05,
  variance_scale = c("display", "unmultiplied")
)

Arguments

x

An asr data frame, an asrs list, or a data frame containing regicode, the selected rate column, and its standard-error or variance column.

event

The event label to report: inci for incidence or mort for mortality.

standard

Standard-population suffix used to find the rate columns. Defaults to wld85. Use cr to compare crude rates.

reference

An external reference table with the same rate and uncertainty columns as x. It may omit regicode when it contains one row. Reference rows are matched using stratum columns shared with x.

rate_col

Optional explicit rate column name. Defaults to asr_standard, or cr when standard is cr.

se_col

Optional explicit standard-error column name. When neither uncertainty-column argument is supplied, existing variance columns are preferred, followed by asr_se_standard or cr_se.

variance_col

Optional explicit variance column name. Used only when se_col is not supplied.

alpha

Two-sided significance level. Defaults to 0.05.

multiplier

Rate multiplier used only when variance_scale = "unmultiplied". Defaults to 100000.

variance_scale

Scale of supplied variance columns. The default, "display", matches current create_asr() output. Use "unmultiplied" for legacy variance columns that have not been multiplied by multiplier^2. Standard-error columns are always interpreted on the displayed rate scale.

Value

A tibble with the target stratum, rate, reference rate, rate difference, rate ratio, log-rate-ratio standard error, z statistic, p_value, confidence limits for the rate ratio, unusual, and status.

Details

The input is normally an object returned by create_asr(..., show_var = TRUE) or create_asr(..., show_se = TRUE). Existing variance columns are preferred when both forms are present. The reference table must contain one matching row for each target stratum.
